title: Pretexts for Sin and the Victory of the Word
english: Men make excuses for their sins alongside those who practice lawlessness. For if my heart were kept by your guarding, I would not be joined with the chosen ones among men who practice lawlessness. And these chosen ones are those who use pretexts upon which they act wickedly, being worse than those without pretexts who lawlessly act without covering. For these are not like those who sin while knowing, who seem to hold ignorance or weakness as a pretext, but like those who lawlessly act while knowing. If, through the things set forth, the one praying says, 'No cause, O Lord, should exist, as if through ignorance, or force, or weakness, that my heart should be turned toward words of wickedness through any pretext upon which one sins,' how might he not also avoid being joined with the chosen ones among men who practice lawlessness? (Ps 140:5b). In this, the ruling principle, as if the head of the soul, must be considered to signify the head.

Understand also this: what else are the chosen ones who practice lawlessness but those in good will, or false doctrines and evil dispositions, whom you would deem worthy of having your own prayer become a means to be exposed and cast out? (Ps 140:5c–8a). For in these things his prayer becomes nothing other than a request to God for their overthrow and destruction. Therefore, regarding his worthiness, manage the matter. For the strong ones among the men practicing lawlessness, being the same as their chosen ones, were crushed, as the divine Scripture has often interpreted the Word of God approaching them as a rock. And a symbol of having conquered is to swallow up; for it is said, 'Death was crushed into victory,' and 'That the mortal might be swallowed up by life,' but also 'Aaron's rod swallowed up theirs'; it says the rods of the sophists and the vainglorious, by the victory of the scepter of divine truth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
